title: Girl dinner
summary: A snack plate that somehow counts as a meal — vibes over macros.
originStory: Started as a tongue-in-cheek TikTok confession: assembling cheese, crackers, leftover fries, and whatever's in the fridge into a 'meal' with zero plating guilt. It snowballed into a celebration of low-effort eating and a gentle pushback on performative wellness. Brands and restaurants briefly tried to monetize it; the internet kept the joke.

title: Roman Empire
summary: The viral bit that men think about Rome 'often' — turned into a culture gag.
originStory: A 2023 TikTok trend asked women how often their partners think about the Roman Empire. Shockingly frequent answers became a meme about hyperfixation, history nerd energy, and gendered conversational weirdness. It spawned endless variants ('what's your Roman Empire?') for any oddly recurring thought.

title: Quiet quitting
summary: Doing your job — not your boss's ambition — without the unpaid overtime.
originStory: Coined in workplace discourse around 2022, 'quiet quitting' reframed boundary-setting as rebellion: meet the job description, skip hustle culture. Critics called it laziness; defenders called it sanity. It rode LinkedIn and TikTok, then cooled as 'quiet luxury' and 'loud quitting' variants took the mic.

title: IYKYK
summary: If You Know, You Know — insider shorthand that gates the joke.
originStory: An abbreviation that signals shared context without explaining it. Used in captions, group chats, and product drops to create belonging (or FOMO). Closely related to 'you had to be there' energy, but shorter and more smug.

title: Skill issue
summary: Gaming roast: the problem isn't the game — it's you.
originStory: Born in competitive gaming chats as a deadpan dismissal of complaints about balance, lag, or 'unfair' mechanics. Migrated to general internet use as a playful (or petty) way to say someone's struggling because of their own ability. Tone ranges from affectionate ribbing to full roast.

title: NPC energy
summary: Acting like a background character — scripted, predictable, unbothered.
originStory: From gaming's non-player characters: entities that repeat lines and follow fixed paths. Online, calling someone an 'NPC' implies they lack originality or agency. The 'NPC meme' wave amplified it into a whole aesthetic of blank stares and canned phrases — sometimes self-deprecating, sometimes cruel.

title: Rizz
summary: Charisma as a verb and a noun — especially flirtation game.
originStory: Short for charisma, popularized by streamer Kai Cenat and Gen Z slang. 'Having rizz' means you can charm; 'unspoken rizz' is magnetism without trying; 'rizzless' is the opposite. Oxford named it Word of the Year in 2023, which only accelerated both adoption and eye-rolls.

title: Corecore
summary: Edit compilations that feel like an existential moodboard with sad audio.
originStory: A TikTok / YouTube edit style stacking unrelated clips — consumerism, loneliness, late-capitalism vibes — into an emotional gut punch. Named as a parody of endless '-core' aesthetics (cottagecore, weirdcore). Less a fashion look, more a feeling delivered via montage.

title: Touch grass
summary: Go outside. Log off. Reconnect with reality (gently or not).
originStory: Internet shorthand telling someone they're too online. Can be caring advice or a dunk. Paired often with 'chronically online.' Originated in meme and gaming spaces, then became mainstream parental and coworker vocabulary — which made the phrase itself feel a little NPC.

title: GG / GG EZ
summary: Good game — or the toxic cousin that gloats after a win.
originStory: 'GG' is polite end-of-match etiquette from competitive gaming. 'GG EZ' (good game, easy) twists it into a taunt. Many communities auto-mute or shame EZ spam. Still, GG alone remains the universal handshake of 'match over, respect.'

title: Delulu
summary: Delusional — but make it aspirational (or chaotic).
originStory: K-pop and stan Twitter shortened 'delusional' into 'delulu,' often about shipping idols or inventing lore. It spilled into mainstream TikTok as 'delulu is the solulu' — joking that believing your own fantasy is a coping strategy. Softened the sting of 'delusional' into something almost cute.

title: FOMO → JOMO
summary: Fear of missing out vs joy of missing out — the pendulum swing.
originStory: FOMO defined social media anxiety for a decade. JOMO flipped it: pleasure in staying home, muting the noise, missing the party on purpose. Both abbreviations still circulate; JOMO peaks whenever burnout discourse does. Trendy exists partly so you can catch the signal without the FOMO spiral.
